detectors.name: Account risk score
detectors.question: Is this account likely automated or fake?
detectors.method: Seven explainable rules (new account < 30 days; < 100 followers; follower/following ratio < 0.2 (when following ≥ 100); > 20 posts/day; default avatar; empty bio; fewer than 5 likes given). Flag when at least 3 rules fire. Rule cut-offs and the minimum count were tuned on the training half only (maximise recall with training FPR ≤ 2.0%).
detectors.split: Stratified 50/50 train/test by account family, seed 42. Numbers below are on the test half.

limits: Twitter-only data from 2014–2016: Bluesky, Telegram or TikTok accounts may behave differently; no labelled set exists for them.
The 'new account' rule never fires here: Cresci bots were months or years old when collected. It is kept because fresh accounts do appear in live swarms (see coordination bench).
The strongest rule here ('almost never likes anything') needs a likes-given count, which X exposes but Bluesky, Telegram and TikTok do not.
Social spambots that imitate humans are the hardest family: see the breakdown.
The rules currently deployed (age < 30 days or < 50 followers) flag 9.2% of genuine humans on this test set: they are shown as weak hints in the UI, never as an alert on their own.

detectors.name: Listed-source referential
detectors.question: Does this link point to state media or a documented influence network?
detectors.method: Exact match (with sub-domains) against a hand-curated list of 23 domains (EU sanctions, VIGINUM, US State Dept, CheckFirst). Nothing was tuned: the list was frozen before this test.
detectors.threshold: Exact match on the domain or a parent domain
detectors.split: No training: every domain is held-out.

limits: Recall on Pravda domains is trivially high: they all share the news-pravda.com parent, which is listed. It checks the matching code, not discovery.
Recall on Iffy+ is low by design: the referential only names state media and documented networks. It is one signal among several, never a verdict on its own.
False positives are near zero, which is what a referential is for: when it fires, it is right.

detectors.name: Coordination detection
detectors.question: Is this story pushed by a coordinated swarm rather than spreading organically?
detectors.method: Production pipeline unchanged: near-duplicate text (MinHash + RapidFuzz) and shared links → stories → explainable signals (copy burst, link burst, new accounts, cross-platform). Alert = level Review or Priority (score ≥ 0.40). Thresholds were fixed before the bench was built.
detectors.split: No training on this bench. Each scenario is injected into 300 real background posts.

datasets.name: Injection bench (synthetic swarms + legitimate viral content)
datasets.note: 240 scenarios, 1716 posts, built with seed 20261114 from 1003 real texts collected for the event 'azov-torture-chambers-nov-2026'.

limits: Synthetic bench: swarms follow scripted patterns. Real operations adapt; recall here is an upper bound.
Precision depends on the mix of swarms and legitimate cases in the bench (5 swarm types, 3 legitimate types, 30 each); the false-alarm rate on legitimate cases is the number to watch.
Paraphrase and translation swarms are not in this bench (the semantic layer is not evaluated here).
Patient swarms of aged accounts spread over days are designed to evade timing rules: expect misses.

detectors.name: Coordinated accounts (account level)
detectors.question: Is this account acting together with other accounts?
detectors.method: Production code unchanged. Coordination network: same own text, same link or same hashtag combination within a window learnt from the data (here 159 s, 10th percentile of re-share delays, CooRnet method); alert = the account has at least one link. Also reported: strong links only (≥ 2 shared actions) and the suspects ranking at level 'likely'.
detectors.threshold: Account linked to ≥ 1 other account in the coordination network
detectors.split: No training. All injected scenarios are mixed together with real background posts.

limits: Synthetic swarms: each injected swarm acts once, so 'strong links' (the same pair acting together again) cannot appear here; in real data they are the most telling signal.
Background accounts are unlabelled: 7.5% of them are linked. Some are real network relays.
Patient swarms spread over days stay below the learnt window: by design they are missed.

known_limits: Scores rank what to check first; they never prove that an account or a source is malicious.
Account data is Twitter 2014–2016; no labelled dataset exists for Bluesky, Telegram or TikTok accounts.
The coordination bench is synthetic; it measures known patterns, not novel tactics.
AI-generated-text detection and semantic (paraphrase) clustering are not evaluated yet.
Confidence intervals are Wilson 95 %; with zero observed errors the upper bound is still above zero.
